title: Tiered Region Indexer: p50/p95 Anomaly Learning & Variant Prioritization
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
Implement a 'Tiered Region Indexer' that selects serving POPs (regions) using both percentile latency telemetry (p50 + p95) and an aggregate network health score. The indexer will be tier-aware (e.g., hosted, dedicated, private) and prioritize fallback model variants when path health degrades. The goal is to reduce tail latency impact for customers while maintaining cost targets and minimizing cross-region churn.

Motivation:
- Current region selection uses mostly p50 or single-signal heuristics which can miss transient tail issues (p95) and packet-loss-related degradations.
- Customers have reported occasional higher p95s despite healthy p50s; this leads to bad UX for latency-sensitive features.
- We need an algorithm that fuses percentile latency with network indicators (pktloss, retransmits, connection error rate) and applies hysteresis+learning to avoid flip-flopping.

Scope / What this ticket covers:
1) Indexer algorithm prototype: combine p50 and p95 into a composite score; apply an additional network health penalty computed from EWMA of packet-loss and TCP timeouts; weight is configurable per customer tier.
2) Anomaly-learning layer: short-term anomaly detector (EWMA + median absolute deviation) to escalate p95 spikes and trigger temporary avoidance of affected POPs.
3) Variant prioritization: maintain prioritized fallback model variants per region (e.g., quantized 8-bit variant, smaller-llm variant) and prefer variants that historically preserved latency under bad network.
4) Tier integration: different weighting / thresholds for Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Private deployments default to conservative avoidance to respect data locality.
5) Observability and dashboards: new metrics and dashboard tiles in Console for composite score, avoidance events, and variant switch rates.
6) Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag with A/B cohorts, canary to 5% then incremental.

Design notes and decisions so far:
- Composite score formula (draft): composite = alpha * normalized(p50) + beta * normalized(p95) + gamma * net_penalty. Default alpha=0.4, beta=0.5, gamma=0.1. Normalization is via a rolling baseline per POP (7d).
- net_penalty = min(1.0, w_loss * loss_ewma + w_timeouts * timeouts_ewma + w_rtt_var * rtt_jitter_ewma). We cap penalty to avoid masking p50 improvements.
- Anomaly escalation: if p95 / baseline_p95 > 2x AND loss_ewma > 0.5%, mark POP in 'degraded' for 2 minutes, increase composite by a fixed multiplier, and trigger variant fallback suggestion.
- Hysteresis: use decay window of 10 minutes before fully restoring a POP to avoid thrash.
- Learning: collect labeled events (avoidance_successful, avoidance_false_positive) to tune beta/gamma per-workload via offline tuning jobs.

Progress updates / timeline:
- 2025-02-10 (Avery Chen): Created ticket after oncall traces showed p95 spikes in eu-west-1 despite stable p50s. Added initial design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Tiered+Region+Indexer+Design
- 2025-02-14 (Diego Martinez): Completed telemetry spike analysis; attached query and example traces in the design doc. Determined net signals to include: packet_loss_ewma, tcp_retransmit_rate, conn_reset_rate, rtt_variance.
- 2025-02-18 (SRE: Priya Nair): Completed infra spike: confirmed metrics available at 1s granularity for POP-level; added metric smoothing pipeline limiter for storage concerns. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/291
- 2025-02-22 (Design review with PM/ENG): Design review notes: PM requested per-customer override on weighting; Design requested UI to explain why a POP was avoided (composite breakdown). Action: add 'explainability' payload to routing decision log.
- 2025-02-25 (Diego): Implemented prototype scorer in branch runtime/feature/region-indexer. Unit tests added for normalization and penalty logic. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4231
- 2025-02-28 (A/B test spike): Canary to 2% traffic in us-east-1 showed one false-positive avoidance where a compute-related backend throttled model variant causing higher p95; we iterated to include model-variant health (serving_queue_depth) in net_penalty.
- 2025-03-04 (Demo): Demoed canary to infra + PM. Metrics: 7% reduction in user-observed p95 for test workload; small +0.6% increase in avg cost due to variant fallback. Recording: https://zoom.redwood.com/recording/1234

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should beta (p95 weight) be for low-latency SLAs vs cost-conscious customers? PM wants per-customer overrides which complicates rollout.
- Inclusion of model-serving internal health signals reduces false positives but ties indexer to runtime internals — for hosted this is ok, for Private we need opt-in. Solution: make model-health signals optional and opt-in per deployment.
- Metric smoothing window size: shorter windows react faster but risk noise; we default 30s with config knob.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before 'Done'):
- Indexer implemented and feature-flagged in runtime.
- Composite score metrics emitted to telemetry with per-pop breakdown.
- Variant-prioritization table stored and used by the routing decision for fallbacks.
- Dashboard shows avoidance events and explains composite breakdown for each decision.
- Can be toggled per-customer and per-deployment with sensible defaults.
- E2E smoke tests validating that when p95 artificially injected, indexer moves traffic appropriately and falls back to prioritized variant.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for normalization and penalty math (coverage target 95% for new code).
- Integration tests using local telemetry generator to simulate p50/p95 divergence and packet loss; verify avoidance/hysteresis behavior.
- Canary in production: 2% -> 10% -> 50% per approval with SLA/metric gates.

Rollout gates / metric thresholds for progression:
- Gate to move from 2% to 10%: no increase in error-rate match (<=0.1%) and decrease in median p95 for cohort >= 3%.
- Gate to move past 10%: cost uplift <= 3% for cohort and avoidance false-positive rate <= 5% over 24h.

Notes for reviewers:
- The prototype PR contains a simple scorer implementation; it's intentionally conservative (beta=0.5). Look for edge cases where normalization baseline can be polluted by one-off incidents.
- Pay attention to explainability: routing logs must include the normalized p50/p95 and net_penalty values for later debugging.
